Series::relu¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::relu() const -> Series
Series& Series::relu_()

What It Does¶

relu() applies the rectified linear unit elementwise:

  • if x > 0, keep x

  • if x <= 0, return 0

So it is a piecewise-linear gate. Negative lanes are shut off, positive lanes pass through unchanged.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series A new Series with the same shape as self, containing the rectified result lane by lane.

Gradient¶

For y = relu(x), the local slope is piecewise:

  • 1 when x > 0

  • 0 when x < 0

At x = 0, the current verified surface also uses 0. That convention is visible directly in the example below.

In-Place Form¶

relu_() is the in-place sibling of relu(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

auto x = pluss::make_series({-1.0, 0.0, 2.0});

auto& ref = x.relu_();
std::cout << "x=" << x << "\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "same object: " << (&ref == &x);

Output¶

x=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 0, 2]
same object: true

Examples¶

Example 1. Negative and zero lanes clamp to zero, while positive lanes survive.

std::cout << pluss::make_series({-2.0, 0.0, 3.0}).relu() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 0, 3]

Example 2. Reverse-mode follows the same gate: off lanes get zero sensitivity, active lanes get one.

auto x = pluss::make_series({-2.0, 0.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

auto y = x.relu();
y.sum().reverse();

std::cout << "out=" << y << "\n";
std::cout << "dL_dx=" << x.sensitivity() << "\n";

Output¶

out=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 0, 3]
dL_dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 0, 1]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • relu() is not smooth at zero.

  • On the current verified surface, the stored slope at exactly zero is 0.

  • This is an elementwise gate, not a reduction or threshold-counting method.

Summary¶

Use relu() when negative lanes should be suppressed and positive lanes should pass through unchanged.

See Also¶

  • Series::sigmoid: smooth bounded gate instead of hard rectification.

  • Series::clamp_min: lower-bound clipping with a configurable floor.
